title: Build a binary search tree in Go with Insert, Contains, InOrder, Min, and Max
description: Greenfield Go task: implement a BST (integer keys) with Insert, Contains, InOrder (sorted slice), Min, and Max operations using recursive tree traversal.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement BST in bst.go.

type BST struct { root *node }
type node struct { key int; left, right *node }

func New() *BST
func (t *BST) Insert(key int)         // no duplicates
func (t *BST) Contains(key int) bool  // search the tree
func (t *BST) InOrder() []int         // in-order traversal → sorted slice
func (t *BST) Min() (int, bool)       // leftmost node; ok=false if empty
func (t *BST) Max() (int, bool)       // rightmost node; ok=false if empty

All 5 tests in bst_test.go must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: BST with root *node; node with key int and left/right *node
Insert rejects duplicates (key already present → no-op)
Contains searches left/right subtree based on key comparison
InOrder returns sorted slice via left-root-right traversal
Min walks leftmost path; Max walks rightmost path
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
